text: Background: BK polyomavirus (BKV) reactivation occurs in 10–30% of kidney transplant recipients and can cause allograft nephropathy. Early virologic monitoring and reduction of immunosuppression remain central to management.

The macrophage paradox in renal AL amyloidosis: lessons from histology and imaging. In renal amyloid light chain amyloidosis, sustained and deep hematologic response drives organ response that continues to improve over time. Rauf et al. demonstrate that macrophage infiltration in kidney biopsies portends progression to renal replacement therapy despite hematologic response, whereas amyloid regression on serum amyloid P component scintigraphy independently predicts favorable outcomes. These findings offer insights into the mechanisms of renal involvement and highlight the complex, context-dependent role of macrophages in amyloid clearance and tissue injury.

Estimating GFR: what it is, what it is not, and why prediction cannot settle the question. Schultheiss et al. show that replacing Chronic Kidney Disease Epidemiology Collaboration with European Kidney Function Consortium cystatin C-based equations reclassifies women, but not men, into milder chronic kidney disease stages, while outcome prediction is unchanged. We argue that prediction of kidney failure cannot validate a glomerular filtration rate equation: dialysis initiation is a clinical decision, not a filtration measurement. The analysis is cross-sectional, leaving longitudinal performance untested. Equations are population tools; at the bedside, non-glomerular filtration rate determinants of both creatinine and cystatin C can mislead.

Microvascular inflammation in kidney transplants: finally an effective treatment? Microvascular inflammation-glomerulitis and peritubular capillaritis-is the hallmark histologic lesion of antibody-mediated allograft rejection and may also occur in the absence of donor-specific antibodies. In either case, microvascular inflammation leads to graft loss, and it has proven difficult to treat. As demonstrated in a study in this issue of Kidney International, targeting CD38, a glycoprotein expressed on both plasma cells and natural killer cells, shows great promise in treating microvascular inflammation in kidney transplants.

Reliability of Spot Urine Protein-to-Creatinine and Urine Albumin-to-Creatinine Ratios in Acute Kidney Injury: A Cohort Study. Spot urine protein-to-creatinine (UPCR) and albumin-to-creatinine (UACR) ratios are common surrogates for 24-hour excretion, but their validity during acute kidney injury (AKI) is uncertain because kidney function is not at steady state. This study assessed the validity of these spot ratios during active AKI compared to after its resolution.

Prescribing patterns and impact of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists in a kidney transplant evaluation cohort in British Columbia, Canada A single-center experience. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RA) have demonstrated weight loss and cardiometabolic benefits in specific subpopulations. Studies of GLP-1RAs in Canadian end-stage renal disease (ESRD) and kidney transplantation (KT) patients are limited.
